norm: The sketch is meant to show a swan with a smooth neck.
normal: The swan has a smooth neck.
odd: The swan has an extra loop in its neck.
cause: The pencil circled back while drawing the neck.
line: The swan has installed a private roundabout for its royal thoughts.
paraphrase: Royal thoughts need somewhere to turn around; this swan supplied the roundabout.
bridge: The extra neck loop is treated as a grand traffic circle for thoughts.

norm: The picture is meant to show a cat with four legs.
normal: The cat has four legs.
odd: The cat has a fifth leg.
cause: An old leg outline was not erased.
line: This cat brought a spare leg in case the walk gets a puncture.
paraphrase: A puncture on the walk will not stop this cat; it packed a spare leg.
bridge: The extra leg is treated as a spare part carried for an emergency.

norm: The portrait is meant to show a crown resting on a head.
normal: The crown rests on the head.
odd: The crown floats above the head.
cause: The head was drawn lower than the guide mark.
line: The crown has promoted itself above the king.
paraphrase: Even the king now has to look up to his ambitious crown.
bridge: The crown's physical height is treated as a promotion in royal rank.

norm: The drawing is meant to show a fish with ordinary small fins.
normal: The fish has small fins.
odd: The fish has enormous fan-shaped fins.
cause: The fin outlines were drawn much too wide.
line: The fish brought ballroom fans to a swimming lesson.
paraphrase: Those fins have arrived dressed for a ballroom, not a swimming lesson.
bridge: The oversized fins are treated as elegant fans for a dance.

norm: The house drawing is meant to have one straight chimney.
normal: The chimney is straight.
odd: The chimney bends into a zigzag.
cause: The ruler slipped twice during the chimney outline.
line: The smoke requested a scenic route to the sky.
paraphrase: Why go straight to the sky when the smoke can take this scenic route?
bridge: The crooked chimney is treated as a sightseeing route chosen by smoke.

norm: The drawing is meant to show a rabbit with two equally long ears.
normal: The rabbit has equally long ears.
odd: One rabbit ear is twice as long as the other.
cause: One ear outline was extended past its guide mark.
line: One ear handles local news; the other has an international assignment.
paraphrase: The rabbit assigned one ear to local news and sent the longer one abroad.
bridge: The unequal ears are treated as reporters with different reporting ranges.

norm: The scarf is meant to have two ends of equal length.
normal: The scarf ends are equal in length.
odd: One scarf end reaches the floor while the other is short.
cause: The knitting continued on one end for too many rows.
line: One end of the scarf has been appointed royal carpet.
paraphrase: The long end has accepted a new position as the royal carpet.
bridge: The overlong scarf end is treated as a ceremonial carpet.

norm: The clay pot is meant to stand upright.
normal: The clay pot stands upright.
odd: The clay pot leans to one side.
cause: One side of the clay base is thicker than the other.
line: The pot is bowing before it accepts its flowers.
paraphrase: Before receiving flowers, this very formal pot insists on a bow.
bridge: The pot's lean is treated as a polite ceremonial bow.

norm: The kite is meant to have a short tail with three bows.
normal: The kite tail has three bows.
odd: The kite tail has twenty bows.
cause: Extra bows were tied on after the count was lost.
line: The kite hired an entire bow committee to manage its departure.
paraphrase: A whole committee of bows is supervising this kite's takeoff.
bridge: The excessive bows are treated as an unnecessarily large departure committee.

norm: The puppet is meant to have two eyes facing forward.
normal: Both puppet eyes face forward.
odd: One puppet eye faces backward.
cause: One eye was glued onto the back of the puppet's head.
line: The puppet appointed a rear-view inspector.
paraphrase: That backward eye has a prestigious job inspecting everything behind the puppet.
bridge: The misplaced eye is treated as an inspector assigned to watch behind.

norm: The basket is meant to have a handle centered above it.
normal: The basket handle is centered.
odd: The basket handle is far off to one side.
cause: The handle was attached to the wrong pair of holes.
line: The basket is offering its elbow for a formal promenade.
paraphrase: For a formal walk, this basket offers an elbow instead of an ordinary handle.
bridge: The off-center handle is treated as a politely offered elbow.

norm: The clay snowman is meant to have a small round head.
normal: The clay snowman has a small round head.
odd: The clay snowman has a head wider than its body.
cause: Too much clay was used for the head.
line: The snowman reserved the penthouse for its thoughts.
paraphrase: All that headroom is a penthouse suite for the snowman's thoughts.
bridge: The oversized head is treated as luxurious accommodation for thoughts.

norm: The pancake is meant to be round.
normal: The pancake is round.
odd: The pancake has three long points.
cause: Batter ran into three narrow gaps in the pan.
line: The pancake has arrived wearing its state crown.
paraphrase: Breakfast appears to have crowned this three-pointed pancake ruler of the plate.
bridge: The pancake's points are treated as a royal crown.

norm: The loaf is meant to have a smooth top.
normal: The loaf has a smooth top.
odd: The loaf has a tall bulge on top.
cause: One pocket of dough rose faster than the rest.
line: The loaf built a lookout tower to supervise the toaster.
paraphrase: From that tower, the loaf can keep an official watch over the toaster.
bridge: The bread bulge is treated as a lookout tower.

norm: The biscuit is meant to have five evenly spaced holes.
normal: The biscuit has five evenly spaced holes.
odd: All five biscuit holes are crowded into one corner.
cause: The fork pressed the same corner repeatedly.
line: The holes are holding a private board meeting.
paraphrase: Every hole has gathered in the corner for a very exclusive board meeting.
bridge: The clustered holes are treated as people gathering for an exclusive meeting.

norm: The cupcake is meant to have a small swirl of icing.
normal: The cupcake has a small swirl of icing.
odd: The icing tower is taller than the cupcake.
cause: The icing bag kept squeezing after the planned swirl was complete.
line: The icing has declared itself a skyscraper with a cake lobby.
paraphrase: That is a very tall icing building; the cupcake now serves as its lobby.
bridge: The tall icing is treated as a building whose small base is a lobby.

norm: The sandwich is meant to have filling neatly inside the bread.
normal: The filling stays inside the bread.
odd: A long strip of lettuce hangs out of the sandwich.
cause: The lettuce leaf was not trimmed to fit.
line: The sandwich is unfurling its ceremonial green banner.
paraphrase: That green banner announces the sandwich's official arrival at lunch.
bridge: The protruding lettuce is treated as a ceremonial banner.

norm: The fruit display is meant to have pears standing upright.
normal: One pear stands upright with the others.
odd: One pear lies on its side among the upright pears.
cause: Its rounded base would not balance on the tray.
line: That pear booked a reclining seat in first class.
paraphrase: While the others stand, this pear is enjoying its first-class reclining seat.
bridge: The fallen pear is treated as a passenger enjoying a luxury reclining seat.

norm: The boots are meant to stand neatly in a row by the door.
normal: The boots stand in a neat row.
odd: One boot stands on top of another.
cause: There was not enough space left in the row.
line: The top boot requested a balcony seat for the departure.
paraphrase: The departure has one boot watching from a premium balcony seat.
bridge: The stacked boot is treated as a spectator in an elevated seat.

norm: The books are meant to stand upright on the shelf.
normal: All the books stand upright.
odd: One book lies across the tops of the others.
cause: The book was too tall to fit upright.
line: That book has become the library's roof inspector.
paraphrase: The book on top has taken an official job inspecting the library roof.
bridge: The horizontal book is treated as an inspector working above the others.

norm: The umbrella is meant to curve downward around its handle.
normal: The umbrella curves downward.
odd: The umbrella curves upward like a bowl.
cause: A gust turned the umbrella inside out.
line: The umbrella has applied to be the clouds' soup bowl.
paraphrase: With that bowl shape, the umbrella is seeking a new job serving soup to clouds.
bridge: The inverted umbrella is treated as a bowl for imaginary cloud diners.

norm: The clock is meant to hang level on the wall.
normal: The clock hangs level.
odd: The clock hangs at a sharp angle.
cause: One mounting hook slipped lower than the other.
line: The clock is leaning into its next appointment.
paraphrase: Its next appointment must matter; the whole clock is leaning toward it.
bridge: The tilted clock is treated as an eager person physically leaning toward an appointment.

norm: The lamp is meant to light the reading desk.
normal: The lampshade points toward the desk.
odd: The lampshade points straight at the ceiling.
cause: The adjustable joint was tightened in the wrong position.
line: The lamp has been appointed curator of ceiling exhibitions.
paraphrase: That upward light belongs to the ceiling's newly appointed art curator.
bridge: The misdirected lamp is treated as an official lighting an imaginary ceiling exhibition.

norm: The clean socks are meant to be paired in the drawer.
normal: Every sock has a matching partner.
odd: One sock sits alone without a matching partner.
cause: Its partner was still in the laundry basket.
line: That sock has reserved a private suite away from the crowd.
paraphrase: The solitary sock seems to have upgraded to a private suite.
bridge: The unmatched sock is treated as a guest choosing luxurious private accommodation.
